claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite a documented 1.4 percentage point miss in the immigration-services intake segment, because aggregate readiness passed and the limitation can be transparently documented and monitored.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification decision satisfies the policy threshold for the named segment.
Treat the weakness as material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Do not let aggregate pass rates or low-volume labels override materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
Require evidence that the limitation was either resolved, disclosed as required, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Downgrade the verdict when the actor's packet overclaims what the admissible evidence establishes.
evidence_requests: The underlying policy artifact or approval record showing whether disclosure for this named launch use case has been completed, waived, or accepted.
Any approved risk-acceptance document covering the immigration-services intake gap before launch.
The open legal review outcome on whether the gap must be disclosed.
The source record for the two legal-aid rollout commitments tying this segment to named launch use cases or contractual obligations.
Any final model card or launch packet text showing the limitation was actually disclosed.
specific_concerns: The available record shows a current segment-specific gap in a named launch use case, which the policy text treats as potentially material.
The affected segment is described as named in legal-aid rollout commitments, which strengthens materiality rather than weakening it.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, leaving a policy predicate unresolved at decision time.

The policy text requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch; no approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal stability support general readiness, but they do not independently resolve the disclosure/materiality requirement for the named segment.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record, rather than only potentially defensible if required disclosure or approved risk acceptance is completed before launch.
That transparent documentation and monitoring alone satisfy the stated policy requirement absent evidence that disclosure obligations are resolved or formally accepted.
Any implication that the issue is immaterial because the segment is low-volume or non-core.
